Implementation Plan

Implementation plan for issue: check-failure triage PR-head routing behind `CHECK_TRIAGE_PR_HEAD_ROUTING_ENABLED` (operator step for #6785)

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends scripts/check_failure_triage.sh
Scope-mode justification: The unblock judge's operator step and the Q1=A answer set the scope: authenticated PR-head routing in the existing triage helper, off by default, wired into the workflow through the existing step `env:` blocks, with paired tests, docs and a changelog fragment. Everything reuses data the helper already fetches. The PR payload from `repos/<repo>/pulls/<n>` at the collect stage is persisted as `pr_payload.json`, and the check SHA arrives as `CHECK_TRIAGE_HEAD_SHA`. So there are no new GitHub API calls (§14), no new scripts or supervisors (§20), and no new external interfaces. The full version (accepted and rejected tests, a defense-in-depth re-check at diagnose, and an exact-one-line validator) costs well under 30 extra LOC over a shortcut. Per §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the plan takes the full version.

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = fedc3891d4dda8097f3b48e111ab645895af16b8, branch `main`. There is no integration-branch metadata, so there is no mismatch.

## Automation surface (§20.E)
- This only modifies existing code. No new script, workflow, cron or supervisor.
- Entry point: the existing `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml` job `triage`, triggered by `check_run: completed` / `workflow_run: completed` through `internal-check-failure-triage.yml` and the consumer wrapper `workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml`. The wrapper doesn't change because the reusable workflow reads the caller repo's `vars`.
- No long-running supervisor. No database work. No `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry.

## Operator prerequisite (blocking for implement, not for this plan)
The issue body does not yet contain a `files_touched:` block. `implement.yml` builds the automation-path grant only from the issue body (`scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py --emit-automation-grant`, which reads the first `files_touched:` block). Before `/approved`, an OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR or the pipeline account must add exactly this block to the issue body:

```
files_touched:
  - scripts/check_failure_triage.sh
  - .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml
  - tests/test_check_failure_triage_workflow_security.py
  - README.md
  - agents.md
  - changelog.d/6785-check-triage-pr-head-routing.md
```

Without it, the `scripts/` and `.github/` edits are rejected again (`guard=automation-path`, `ai:scope-blocked`). That is the same failure as #6785.

## 1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh`: flag, verification at collect, re-verification at diagnose, appending the routing line, and the final body validator.
- `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml`: add the flag to the `env:` of steps "Collect check-failure context" and "Diagnose check failure".
- `tests/test_check_failure_triage_workflow_security.py`: behavioural and contract tests.
- `README.md`: new row in the variables table next to `CHECK_FAILURE_TRIAGE_MAX_LINEAGE_DEPTH` (around line 2087).
- `agents.md`: one or two sentences in workflow-architecture item 13, "check failure triage".
- `changelog.d/6785-check-triage-pr-head-routing.md` (new), following CLAUDE.md §20 fragment rules.

No other file. The post step ("Post check-failure triage issue") does not change. It only checks the fp marker and truncates at 60,000 chars, and the routing line sits in the header, so truncation keeps it.

## 2. Functions / modules to implement
All of this goes in `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh`, using tabs and opening braces on a new line, as the file already does.

a) Config. Next to `ENABLED=...` (around line 122):
   `PR_HEAD_ROUTING_ENABLED="${CHECK_TRIAGE_PR_HEAD_ROUTING_ENABLED:-false}"`. Routing is on only when the lowercased value is exactly `true`. Any other value means off. Document it in the header's "Optional env" list. Initialize `ROUTING_HEAD_REF=""`.

b) New helper `triage_routing_unverified()` taking `<detail>`, where detail is a fixed token, never untrusted text:
   - `log "outcome=skip reason=routing_unverified detail=${1} pr=${PR_NUMBER}"`. This gives the stable line `CHECK_TRIAGE outcome=skip reason=routing_unverified ...`.
   - `tg_send_msg "Check-failure auto-triage skipped ${REPO} PR #${PR_NUMBER}: PR-head routing could not be verified (${1}). No issue was filed."$'\n'"Run: ${RUN_URL}" "WARNING" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`, which fails open. Do not put the head ref or PR title in the message.
   - `exit 0`. Exit before `GITHUB_OUTPUT ready=true` is written, so the diagnose and post steps are skipped.

c) New helper `triage_valid_routing_ref()` taking `<ref>`. It returns 0 only when all of these hold:
   - the ref is nonempty and at most 255 bytes;
   - it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$`. This is stricter than git, so the ref cannot contain backticks, whitespace or newlines. That matters because `resolve_integration_ref.sh`'s regex `([^`\n]+?)` and the display path would break on those characters.
   - `git check-ref-format --branch "${ref}" >/dev/null 2>&1` succeeds.

d) Collect-stage verification. Insert it right after the existing `pr_not_open` / `fork_pr` gates (around line 265), before lineage, label and context work, so an unverifiable run costs no further API calls or model work. It runs only when the flag is on. Fail closed on each condition, in this order:
   - The PR fetch failed or returned invalid JSON. The current code then sets `PR_JSON='{}'` and "proceeds with minimal context". With the flag on, this becomes `detail=pr_unreadable`. Track the state with a local flag set in the existing fetch branches, not with a new API call.
   - `PR_STATE != open`, including empty: `pr_not_open`.
   - `HEAD_REPO_FULL_NAME` is empty or not equal to `REPO`: `head_repo_mismatch`.
   - `triage_valid_routing_ref "${HEAD_REF}"` fails: `head_ref_invalid`.
   - `PR_HEAD_SHA="$(... jq -r '.head.sha // ""')"`. If it or `HEAD_SHA` is empty, or either doesn't match `^[0-9a-f]{40}$`: `head_sha_missing`.
   - `PR_HEAD_SHA != HEAD_SHA`: `head_sha_mismatch`.
   On success, set `ROUTING_HEAD_REF="${HEAD_REF}"` and `log "routing verified pr=${PR_NUMBER}"`.
   With the flag off, this block is skipped entirely and behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged.

e) Metadata. The collect-stage `jq -n` that writes `triage_metadata.json` gains `--arg routing_head_ref "${ROUTING_HEAD_REF}"` and the field `routing_head_ref: $routing_head_ref`. The field is empty when the flag is off. The other keys stay as they are (§10, additive only).

f) Diagnose-stage re-verification. This is defense in depth with no API call. In the `TRIAGE_STAGE = diagnose` metadata block, read `ROUTING_HEAD_REF="$(jq -r '.routing_head_ref // ""' ...)"`. The `// ""` keeps older metadata files working. Then, only when the flag is on, before the model runs:
   - Run `triage_valid_routing_ref` on it, else `metadata_mismatch`.
   - It must equal `pr_payload.json` `.head.ref`, `.state == "open"` and `.head.repo.full_name == REPO`, else `metadata_mismatch`.
   - `pr_payload.json` `.head.sha` must equal `CHECK_TRIAGE_HEAD_SHA` and both must be 40-hex, else `head_sha_mismatch`.
   When the flag is off, force `ROUTING_HEAD_REF=""`, so a leftover field never routes. For `TRIAGE_STAGE=all`, ROUTING_HEAD_REF is already set in-process by (d).

g) Composition. In the `BODY_FILE` block, only when `ROUTING_HEAD_REF` is nonempty, the script itself writes `- **Integration branch:** \`${ROUTING_HEAD_REF}\`` as a list item right after the `- **Head SHA:**` line. That is the trusted header above the first `---`, before the neutralized diagnosis. Model text never supplies it. The neutralizer has already rewritten any model or log `Integration branch:` to `(untrusted)`. This format matches `resolve_integration_ref.sh`'s `^\s*(?:-\s*)?(?:\*\*Integration branch:\*\*|Integration branch:)\s*`?\s*([^`\n]+?)\s*`?\s*$`.

h) Final body validation, in the existing Python heredoc around line 668. Pass `"${ROUTING_HEAD_REF}"` as a new argv[6]. Keep the marker and reissue checks as they are. Replace the single `any(key.match(...))` with:
   - `matches_nl` = indices of lines in `body.split("\n")` matching the routing-key regex. `matches_uni` = the same over `body.splitlines()`. Both are needed so Unicode line separators can't hide or duplicate a line.
   - If argv[6] is empty, any match prints `routing_key`. This is today's behaviour.
   - If argv[6] is nonempty, each of `matches_nl` and `matches_uni` must contain exactly one match. That one line must match the resolver's exact Integration-branch regex, its capture group must equal argv[6], and it must appear before the first `---` line. Otherwise print `routing_key`.
   - Also check that argv[6] passes the same `^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$` check inside Python.
   The existing failure path is unchanged: `body_validation_failed`, a CRITICAL alert and `exit 1`. That path covers model or validator faults. "Routing could not be verified" uses the WARNING skip path in (b).

i) No change to the direct-caller `gh issue create` path apart from it inheriting the validated body.

## 3. Data structures affected
- `triage_metadata.json` gains the field `routing_head_ref` (string, empty when routing is off or unverified). The change is additive. Readers use `// ""`, and the post step reads only `fingerprint`, `generation` and `root`.
- The issue body gains at most one header line, `- **Integration branch:** \`<ref>\``, and only when the flag is on and routing was verified.
- New stable log lines under the existing `CHECK_TRIAGE` prefix: `outcome=skip reason=routing_unverified detail=<pr_unreadable|pr_not_open|head_repo_mismatch|head_ref_invalid|head_sha_missing|head_sha_mismatch|metadata_mismatch> pr=<n>` and `routing verified pr=<n>`. No new prefix, so the agents.md LOG_PRE
